title: Declare cryptography as a test dependency so the end-to-end TLS tests execute in CI
objective: Make the two end-to-end TLS tests in tests/unit/test_ingest_fetch.py actually execute in CI by declaring cryptography as a test dependency, without altering any production behaviour, and prove the coverage hole is closed by mutation rather than by assertion.
defect: test_https_certificate_is_verified_against_the_hostname_end_to_end and test_https_still_rejects_a_certificate_for_a_different_hostname are guarded by pytest.importorskip("cryptography"). cryptography is not in the dev extra, so pip install -e ".[dev]" does not supply it and BOTH tests skip in CI. A Level-2 evaluator built the break rather than arguing it: two defects (M1, weakening the injected ssl context; M3, retrying unverified on an SSL error) fully defeat certificate verification while leaving server_hostname, check_hostname and CERT_REQUIRED exactly as the standard-library-only test asserts, so both stay GREEN in CI. Only the skipped end-to-end tests catch them. The shipped code is CORRECT; this is purely a coverage gap.
approach: Declare cryptography in BOTH pyproject.toml [project.optional-dependencies].dev and requirements-dev.txt, which are mirrored by contract and must move together.
Change nothing else: no production code, no test logic, no removal of the importorskip guards (they remain correct fallbacks for a developer without the extra installed).
Correct the now-false section comment in tests/unit/test_ingest_fetch.py that asserts cryptography is not a declared test dependency and that these tests skip in CI.
in_scope: tests/unit/test_ingest_fetch.py (section comment only; no test logic)
docs/TEST_STRATEGY.md (only if still overstated after the change)
out_of_scope_zero_diff: apps/api/app/ingest/fetch.py -- this slice adds coverage and must not alter behaviour
apps/api/app/ingest/adapters/** and tests/fixtures/** (a concurrent slice owns them)
apps/api/requirements.txt and apps/worker/requirements.txt (production surfaces; cryptography is a TEST dependency and must not reach a shipped image)
promotion or merge of the draft pull request
acceptance_criteria: A1: cryptography is declared in requirements-dev.txt AND pyproject.toml dev extra with the same pin, so the mirrored files do not drift.
A2: The CI skip count drops from 4 to 2, and the two remaining skips are confirmed by name to be the pre-existing tests/integration/test_stack_health.py stack-health tests rather than assumed.
A3: THE TEST THAT MATTERS -- mutant M1 (weaken the injected ssl context) makes the suite RED with cryptography installed.
A4: Mutant M3 (retry unverified when an SSL error occurs) makes the suite RED with cryptography installed.
A5: Mutant M2 (verify against the IP literal instead of the hostname) is STILL caught, proving the standard-library-only test was not weakened.
A6: Every mutant is restored byte-exactly, proven by git hash-object against git rev-parse ref:path -- never by numstat.
A7: The pinned cryptography version carries no known advisory, verified by running the same auditor CI runs (pip-audit 2.9.0).

A8: pip-audit -r requirements-dev.txt acquires NO NEW finding. The audit output is captured before and after and compared precisely; a new genuine advisory is a STOP-and-report condition, not something to work around.
A9: Zero diff to every protected path; agent-state/feature_list.json byte-identical to base and no flag flipped.
A10: The full suite passes and the measured pass/skip figures are recorded from THIS run, not copied from a prior entry.
verification_plan: Measure the baseline: install -e ".[dev]" into a clean virtual environment, confirm cryptography is absent, and record the skip count and skip names.
Capture pip-audit -r requirements-dev.txt output BEFORE the change.
Apply the dependency declaration to both mirrored files.
Capture pip-audit -r requirements-dev.txt output AFTER the change and diff the two precisely.
Re-run the suite with cryptography present and record the new skip count and names.
Reproduce M1, M3 and M2 one at a time, stating the prediction before measuring, and record the measured outcome for each.
Restore each mutant and prove restoration by blob hash.
Verify the docs/TEST_STRATEGY.md TLS sentence has become accurate.
Commit, push, open a DRAFT pull request, and inspect CI.
negative_tests: M1: LiveFetcher._ssl_context returns a context with check_hostname off and verify_mode CERT_NONE -- must be caught.
M3: LiveFetcher._open retries with an unverified context when ssl.SSLError is raised -- must be caught.
M2: the pinned handler verifies against the dialled IP literal instead of the hostname -- must remain caught by the standard-library-only test.
data_implications: None. No persisted row, migration, CHECK constraint, fixture or provider classification changes in this slice.
security_privacy: Security coverage only. The dependency is a TEST dependency and is deliberately NOT added to apps/api/requirements.txt or apps/worker/requirements.txt, so the shipped runtime image surface is unchanged. Adding cryptography does widen the audited development surface that pip-audit gates on, which is why the audit is measured before and after rather than assumed neutral. The test generates a throwaway key into a pytest temporary directory that is never committed, so no credential enters the tree.
portability: cryptography publishes manylinux and macOS/Windows wheels for CPython 3.13 on amd64 and arm64, so no source build is imposed on any supported platform. No new mandatory service. Production runtime dependencies are unchanged.
z0_risk: No runtime Z0 change. No classifier, publication or catalogue behaviour is touched.
known_ci_exception: The Dependency audit check is red on advisory GHSA-2v37-7h3g-55p8 (nanoid <3.3.18) in apps/web on current origin/main as well, through no code change, because npm audit queries the live advisory database at run time. That failure is pre-existing, Node-side and unrelated to this Python-side change. It does NOT excuse a new finding: the Python development audit is measured before and after specifically to distinguish the two.
